stories.headline: Ebola outbreak in DRC is spreading faster than containment efforts
stories.summary: UN News reports more than 900 suspected cases and 220 suspected deaths from the Bundibugyo strain of Ebola in the Democratic Republic of the Congo, with WHO warning that community distrust, conflict, treatment-centre attacks, and cross-border risk are complicating response efforts.
stories.pastoral_note: Pray for courage and protection for health workers, wisdom for local leaders, and mercy for grieving families. This is also a sobering reminder that misinformation is not abstract; it can become life-and-death discipleship around truth, trust, and neighbour-love.

stories.headline: Gunmen kill three Christians at prayer vigil in western Nigeria
stories.summary: Morning Star News reports that gunmen attacked a church prayer vigil in Kwara state on May 23, killing three Christians and abducting 15 others. The attack adds to a wider pattern of violence against Christian communities in Nigeria this spring.
stories.pastoral_note: Hold persecuted believers before the Lord by name where possible, and remind the church that prayer meetings are not small things; in many places they are acts of costly allegiance to Jesus.

stories.headline: Gen Z and Gen Alpha show signs of pushing back against doomscrolling
stories.summary: A Mastercard report says younger generations are increasingly seeking agency over digital life: focusing on micro-communities, co-creating culture instead of passively consuming it, and, according to GWI data cited in the piece, 40% of 12- to 15-year-olds worldwide take screen-time breaks for digital self-care.
stories.pastoral_note: This is a discipleship opening. The next generation may not need another lecture about phones as much as a compelling vision of embodied community, Sabbath, attention, and meaningful participation in the life of God.

stories.headline: Tech companies are asking faith leaders to help shape AI ethics
stories.summary: AP reports that representatives from major AI companies and multiple religious traditions met for the first Faith-AI Covenant roundtable in New York, aiming to develop moral norms for rapidly advancing AI systems. The initiative reflects a notable shift from Silicon Valley skepticism toward organized religion to seeking faith-based ethical wisdom.
stories.pastoral_note: The church should enter this conversation neither dazzled nor defensive. Scripture gives us categories AI cannot generate on its own: image of God, wisdom, agency, creatureliness, truth, and love of neighbour.

stories.headline: HBR: Great teams keep learning, even when things are working
stories.summary: Harvard Business Review’s May-June issue highlights Ron Friedman’s research-backed argument that high-performing teams become resilient through continuous improvement: curiosity, early problem-surfacing, experimentation, feedback that supports learning, and growth tied to shared meaning rather than perfection.
stories.pastoral_note: Healthy church teams need the same posture: not frantic reinvention, but humble learning. Theologically, this sounds like sanctification in community: truthful feedback, grace for mistakes, and shared mission over ego.

stories.headline: Fraser Valley market shows early stabilization while buyers retain selection
stories.summary: The Fraser Valley Real Estate Board’s April 2026 report says benchmark prices edged upward for a second consecutive month, sales rose month-over-month and year-over-year for the first annual increase in more than a year, and elevated inventory continues to create favourable conditions for buyers.
stories.pastoral_note: For Fraser Valley families, housing remains both financial pressure and pastoral reality. Keep praying for renters, young families, downsizers, and those making major decisions under affordability stress.

stories.headline: Kidnapped priest released amid rare local resistance to attacks in Nigeria
stories.summary: Morning Star News reports that a kidnapped priest was released and some Fulani attacks on Christian communities in Nigeria were partially thwarted, even as violence in Kogi and Plateau states remained severe. The story holds grief and hope together rather than offering an easy victory narrative.
stories.pastoral_note: This is a good moment to teach the church how to pray with both lament and thanksgiving: mourning the dead, asking for justice, and celebrating every rescue as a mercy of God.

stories.headline: Pew: More Americans say religion is gaining influence, but remain wary of politicized faith
stories.summary: Pew Research Center finds 37% of U.S. adults now say religion is gaining influence in American life, the highest share since 2002, while 61% still say it is losing influence. More than half view religion’s social influence positively, but many want houses of worship to stay out of day-to-day partisan politics.
stories.pastoral_note: The evangelistic edge is clear: people are not done with God, but they are suspicious of power dressed up as faith. Preach Jesus as King without reducing the kingdom to a voting bloc; let holiness, mercy, and truth make the gospel plausible again.
